title: Controller (full-time)
triggerSummary: Hire a full-time Controller when controller coverage is not already full-time. This is the first finance hire because close, audit readiness, and financial controls all stall without it.
outcomes: Monthly close completed on a published calendar with reviewed reconciliations
Written accounting policies and technical positions the auditor can rely on
Payables, receivables, and payroll accounting operating under documented control
Audit readiness owned end to end so the CFO is not doing accounting work
scorecard: Has closed the books at a company of similar or greater complexity
Has taken a company through a first external audit
Can write a revenue recognition memo without external help
Has built a close calendar and reduced close cycle time with evidence
Has hired and developed at least one accountant
Comfortable operating without a large team or mature systems
interviewQuestions: Walk me through the close you ran most recently, day by day, and tell me where it broke.
Describe a revenue recognition judgment you made that the auditor initially challenged. How did it end?
You inherit a balance sheet with several unsupported accounts. What do you do in the first two weeks?
How would you cut close from twelve days to six without adding headcount?
Tell me about a control failure you found. How did you find it and what did you change?

title: Fractional or outsourced Controller
triggerSummary: Use fractional or outsourced controller coverage as an interim step when there is no controller at all and revenue does not yet justify a full-time senior hire.
outcomes: Close runs on a defined calendar within weeks rather than months
Immediate remediation of the highest-risk accounting gaps
A documented handover package for the eventual full-time controller
scorecard: Available for a defined weekly commitment, not on an ad hoc basis
Has run close at multiple venture-backed companies
Willing to document work for handover rather than retain knowledge
Fixed scope and fee rather than open-ended hourly billing
interviewQuestions: How many days per week can you commit and which days are they?
What does your handover package look like when a full-time controller starts?
Which parts of close will you do yourself and which will you supervise?
How do you handle a close that is at risk of missing the deadline?

title: Strategic Finance and Planning Lead
triggerSummary: Hire strategic finance once controller coverage exists. This role owns the model, the plan, the forecast, and board analytics so the CFO stops being the only analyst.
outcomes: One integrated three-statement model that the board and executive team trust
A monthly rolling forecast with a documented change log
Budget versus actual reporting that budget owners use and explain
Board analytics produced without the CFO rebuilding them
scorecard: Builds three-statement models from scratch without templates
Has run a full annual planning cycle to board approval
Can explain unit economics and cohort analysis clearly to non-finance leaders
Comfortable partnering directly with sales, marketing, and engineering leaders
Strong data skills beyond spreadsheets
interviewQuestions: Build me the revenue driver structure for our business model out loud.
How do you decide whether a forecast miss is a timing issue or a structural problem?
Describe how you ran a planning cycle. Where did it go wrong and what did you change?
How would you present a downside scenario to a board that does not want to hear it?

title: Senior Accountant
triggerSummary: Add accounting capacity when the controller is performing transaction-level work personally, which is signalled by fewer than two staff accountants at this revenue scale.
outcomes: Close tasks, reconciliations, and subledger work executed to the calendar
Payables, receivables, and payroll accounting handled without controller intervention
Audit support schedules prepared and indexed
scorecard: Has prepared complete balance sheet reconciliations independently
Comfortable with high transaction volume and system-driven accounting
Accurate and fast on repeatable work without needing reminders
Has supported an external audit as a preparer
interviewQuestions: Walk me through how you reconcile a deferred revenue account.
Describe a reconciliation difference you could not resolve. What did you do?
How do you organize your work during close week?
What have you automated in your previous role and how?

title: Finance Operations and Systems Lead
triggerSummary: Hire finance systems ownership when the company is still on entry-level accounting software at scale, because the migration and integration work needs a dedicated owner.
outcomes: A documented systems architecture with automated data flow between systems
Accounting system migration delivered with reconciled data and a parallel run
Payables, expense, procurement, and payroll workflows automated with audit trails
Quarterly access reviews and master data governance operating
scorecard: Has implemented or migrated a mid-market accounting system end to end
Understands accounting well enough to design the chart of accounts and integrations
Has built integrations between billing, payroll, and accounting systems
Manages vendors and implementation partners firmly on scope and timeline
interviewQuestions: Describe a system migration you led. What went wrong and how did you recover?
How do you decide whether to configure the system or change the process?
How would you validate that migrated data is correct before cut-over?
Which finance processes would you automate first here and why?

title: Revenue Operations and Commercial Finance Manager
triggerSummary: Add commercial finance when revenue scale makes pricing, deal desk, commissions, and quote-to-cash a full-time job rather than a CFO side activity.
outcomes: Deal desk operating with published approval limits and fast turnaround
Commission calculations produced accurately on schedule with few disputes
Quote-to-cash running without manual re-keying between systems
Pricing and unit economics analysis available for every commercial decision
scorecard: Has run a deal desk or commercial approval process at a growing company
Can model pricing and packaging changes including churn risk
Understands revenue recognition consequences of commercial terms
Has administered commission plans and resolved disputes
interviewQuestions: Walk me through how you would review a non-standard deal in under a day.
How do you set discount approval limits that speed up rather than slow down selling?
Describe a pricing change you analyzed. What happened after it launched?
How do you keep a sales team trusting your commission numbers?

title: Billing and Collections Specialist
triggerSummary: Add dedicated billing and collections capacity when usage-based or hybrid billing volume makes invoicing and cash application a daily operational job.
outcomes: Invoices issued accurately and on schedule with disputes resolved quickly
Cash applied within days of receipt with unapplied balances cleared monthly
Aged receivables worked weekly against a defined collections sequence
scorecard: Has managed a high-volume invoicing cycle including usage-based charges
Comfortable working directly with customers on payment conversations
Detail-oriented with proven accuracy on invoice preparation
Has used a billing platform rather than only spreadsheets
interviewQuestions: How do you verify that a usage-based invoice is correct before it is sent?
Describe how you handle a customer who has not paid for sixty days.
What is your process when a customer disputes part of an invoice?
How do you reduce the number of invoices that get disputed in the first place?

title: Technical Accounting Manager
triggerSummary: Add technical accounting capability when an audit is under way or imminent and complex judgment areas need documented positions.
outcomes: Auditor-ready memos covering every significant judgment area
Audit requests answered without diverting the controller from close
Complex transactions assessed for accounting impact before they are signed
scorecard: Public accounting background with technical accounting depth
Has written memos that survived audit review with limited revision
Current on the standards relevant to this business model
Writes clearly enough that non-accountants can follow the conclusion
interviewQuestions: Take our most complex contract type and talk me through the revenue analysis.
How do you document a judgment where the answer is genuinely arguable?
Describe a time the auditor disagreed with your position. What happened?
How do you decide when an issue needs external technical accounting advice?

title: Payroll and Equity Administrator
triggerSummary: Add dedicated payroll and equity administration once headcount makes multi-state or multi-country payroll and equity events a recurring specialist workload.
outcomes: Payroll processed accurately and on time across every jurisdiction
Equity grants, exercises, and terminations recorded and reconciled promptly
Payroll tax registrations and filings kept current in every state
scorecard: Has run multi-state payroll and understands registration requirements
Has administered an equity plan including exercises and terminations
Handles confidential compensation data with discretion
Meticulous about deadlines and reconciliation detail
interviewQuestions: An employee moves to a new state mid-quarter. What do you do?
Walk me through processing an option exercise for a departing employee.
How do you check a payroll register before you transmit it?
Describe a payroll error you found before it was paid. How did you find it?

title: Treasury Manager
triggerSummary: Add treasury capability when the cash balance and banking structure make daily cash management, investment policy execution, and covenant reporting a standing workload.
outcomes: Daily cash position produced and reviewed without CFO involvement
The 13-week forecast maintained weekly with measured accuracy
Investment policy executed with documented compliance reporting
Banking relationships and fraud controls actively managed
scorecard: Has built and maintained a direct-method cash forecast
Understands short-term investment instruments and their liquidity profile
Has managed banking relationships and implemented fraud controls
Detail-oriented about daily reconciliation and exception follow-up
interviewQuestions: How do you build a 13-week forecast and how do you improve its accuracy?
How would you structure our accounts and sweeps given our balance and burn?
What fraud controls would you insist on with our banks?
Describe how you would report policy compliance to the board.

title: Tax Lead (outsourced or fractional)
triggerSummary: Engage outsourced tax capability when there is no internal tax coverage and the multi-state footprint creates real filing and nexus obligations.
outcomes: Every filing obligation identified, calendared, and met
Nexus exposure quantified and remediated on agreed terms
Research credit and other available benefits claimed with documentation
Provision support delivered on the audit timeline
scorecard: Experience with venture-backed companies at similar scale
Multi-state sales tax and voluntary disclosure experience
Research credit study capability with defensible documentation
Responsive on notices within days rather than weeks
interviewQuestions: How would you approach our multi-state nexus exposure and what would you do first?
Walk me through how you document a research credit claim so it survives examination.
How do you coordinate with our auditor on provision timing?
What is your response time commitment when a state notice arrives?

title: Internal Audit and Controls Lead
triggerSummary: Add controls and internal audit capability at larger scale, where control failures become material and future reporting requirements need a multi-year readiness plan.
outcomes: A documented key controls matrix mapped to the risk register
A control testing program with evidence and tracked remediation
A phased readiness plan for future public company requirements
scorecard: Internal audit or control testing experience in a growth environment
Can distinguish controls that matter from controls that only create work
Has driven remediation to closure through other functions
Communicates findings without creating defensiveness
interviewQuestions: Which five controls would you test first here and why those five?
How do you handle a control owner who disagrees with your finding?
Describe a control you recommended removing rather than adding.
How would you phase readiness work over three years rather than one?

title: Finance Data and Business Intelligence Analyst
triggerSummary: Add finance data capability once reporting and metric production consume analyst time that should be spent on analysis, typically alongside a warehouse or reporting layer build.
outcomes: Governed finance data models with documented lineage and tests
Self-service dashboards for budget owners and executives
Metric definitions implemented consistently across every report
scorecard: Strong data modeling and query skills alongside finance literacy
Has built dashboards that people actually used rather than requested
Understands data quality testing and can explain a broken number
Works well with data engineering and analytics teams
interviewQuestions: How would you model our revenue data so billing and the ledger reconcile?
Describe a dashboard you built that changed a decision.
How do you handle two systems that report different numbers for one metric?
What tests would you put on a finance data pipeline?

title: International Finance Capability
triggerSummary: Add international finance capability, usually through local advisors first, once the company employs people outside its home country and needs local statutory and payroll compliance.
outcomes: Local statutory accounts and filings completed in every country of operation
Local payroll and employment compliance maintained
Transfer pricing and intercompany arrangements documented and executed
A clear view of the cost and obligations of each country footprint
scorecard: Coverage in every country where the company has people or entities
Experience with venture-backed subsidiaries rather than only large corporates
Can coordinate with the parent company auditor and tax preparer
Transparent fixed-fee scope per country rather than open-ended billing
interviewQuestions: Which countries do you cover directly and which through partners?
What are the statutory audit thresholds in the countries where we operate?
How do you coordinate local statutory accounts with our consolidated reporting?
What does your annual cost look like per country at our size?
